question.problem:
$$
{f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,4)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{{x}^{3/2}}, & \,4\le x\le 9 \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Let $X$ and $Y$ be continuous random variables. 
Find the conditional variance $\text{Var}[X\,|\,Y=4]$ given that the conditional probability density function ${f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,4)$ is shown above and the corresponding expected value is ${\mu }_{X|4}=6.$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that the conditional variance of $X$ given $Y=y$ is defined by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X\,|\,Y=y] & =\text{E}[(X-{\mu }_{X|y})^{2}\,|\,Y=y] \\  & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}\,|\,Y=y]-{\mu }_{X|y}^{2},\end{aligned}
$$

where 

$$
\text{E}[{X}^{2}\,|\,Y=y]={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }{x}^{2}\,{f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,y)\,\text{d}x.
$$

Therefore, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}\,|\,Y=4] & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }{x}^{2}\,{f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,4)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{4}^{9}{x}^{2}\cdot \frac{3}{{x}^{3/2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{4}^{9}3\sqrt{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[2{x}^{3/2}]}_{4}^{9} \\  & =2(27-8) \\  & =38.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X\,|\,Y=4] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}\,|\,Y=4]-{\mu }_{X|4}^{2} \\  & =38-{6}^{2} \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$
